content.title: About
content.content: Grated Parmesan is a hard, aged cheese made from cow's milk, produced in Italy following traditional methods. In its refrigerated form it is kept at 2‑4 °C, preserving its aroma and texture. Parmesan offers a sharp, nutty flavor with a slightly salty finish and a granular consistency.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Parmesan (Parmigiano‑Reggiano) holds Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) status.
The milk must come from cows fed only on grass and hay.
The cheese is aged a minimum of 12 months, often 24‑36 months, which deepens its flavor.
Grated Parmesan is a staple topping for pasta, risotto, and salads in Italian cuisine.
Hard Parmesan contains over 30 % dry matter, of which about 30 % is protein.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Parmesan provides roughly 1,100 mg of calcium per 100 g, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: It supplies about 35 g of complete whey protein per 100 g.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The cheese is a good source of vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains zinc and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals aid immune function and energy production.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: Extended aging breaks down most lactose, making Parmesan generally well‑tolerated by those with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to Parmesan.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Parmesan contains about 650 mg of sodium per 100 g, which can be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: It provides roughly 430 kcal per 100 g, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Those prone to gout should monitor intake due to purines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sprinkle grated Parmesan over hot dishes such as pasta, risotto, or soups at the end of cooking to melt and release flavor. Use it as a topping for salads, casseroles, and roasted vegetables. It can be mixed with olive oil and herbs for a tasty dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in an airtight container. Once opened, use within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if it develops an ammonia smell or off‑color.
